page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance designed for parallel computing, AI inference, and memory-intensive enterprise tasks. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running on the KVM hypervisor, providing 32 x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz with one thread per core. The hardware implementation includes vector and cryptographic extensions such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX512-BF16, and VAES. System memory totals 384 GB of RAM, offering a high allocation of 12 GB per core.

Hardware acceleration is delivered via three discrete NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs providing a cumulative 144 GB of GDDR6 VRAM. In synthetic tests, the triple-GPU array achieves prompt processing rates of 13,662.51 tokens per second on lightweight 135M language models and 6,061.83 tokens per second on 7B parameter models, with text generation throughput reaching 129.38 tokens per second on 7B architectures. Local storage is not bundled with the instance, requiring network-attached storage volumes for operational file systems and persistent datasets.

General-purpose benchmark results place the instance in high performance brackets. The system recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 27,001 and a single-core score of 3,003, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 87,724.35 and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 132,459.57. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 331.99 GB/sec with write speeds of 123.17 GB/sec, while in-memory operations demonstrated 128.07 million Redis SET operations per second.

The combination of 144 GB of GPU memory, high memory density per core, and advanced matrix instructions makes this configuration suited for AI model inference, computer vision processing, 3D rendering pipelines, and parallel data transformations where attached storage can be provisioned externally.
description: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-3xL40S is an enterprise GPU-accelerated instance configured with 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor and 384 GB of system RAM. Hardware acceleration is provided by three NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs delivering 144 GB of combined VRAM. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-tier results, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 27,001, PassMark CPU score of 87,724.35, and 6,061.83 tokens per second in 7B LLM prompt processing. Memory bandwidth reaches 331.99 GB/sec for large sequential reads. The instance includes one public IPv4 address and does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating network storage attachments for persistent workloads. This hardware composition is tailored for large-scale AI inference, graphics processing, ray tracing, and compute-heavy data engineering.
